title: Aurora PostgreSQL compute and shared distributed storage
description: Simplified read path for a provisioned Aurora PostgreSQL instance. Persistent data is in an SSD-backed shared distributed cluster volume. Cache hits do not take this storage path; eligible local Optimized Reads caches are omitted. Geometry is schematic, not measured capacity, network distance or latency. Availability zones and replication are outside the visual scope. Visible io2/gp3 latency values are illustrative EBS references, not measurements of Aurora or isolated network-hop latency.

stages.name: today
stages.heading: AWS Aurora Postgres architecture
stages.description: Memory serves cached pages. Reads requiring Aurora persistent storage cross the storage network to its shared cluster volume.

stages.name: scale-up
stages.heading: Scale up → Network Hop remains
stages.description: A larger provisioned DB instance supplies more CPU, memory and potentially network bandwidth. Independently, the shared volume automatically grows as data increases. Shapes illustrate vertical compute scaling and data growth, not a manual EBS IOPS or SSD upgrade. The storage placement remains remote. The taller host, CPU, memory and SSD frames illustrate more capacity; the network connection remains in place. SSD storage is Aurora’s shared cluster volume, not an attached EBS volume.

stages.name: storage-waits
stages.heading: Bottleneck → Network Hop for Storage I/O
stages.description: A conditional I/O-bound workload: physical storage waits can raise query tail latency and reduce completed work at a given concurrency. More memory and tuning may help; an unchanged network hop does not imply an unchanged measured latency.
